s: A software company hosts an application on AWS with resources in multiple AWS accounts and Regions. The application runs on a group of Amazon EC2 instances in an application VPC located in the us-east-1 Region with an IPv4 CIDR block of 10.10.0.0. In a different AWS account, a shared services VPC is located in the us-east-2 Region with an IPv4 CIDR block of 10.10.10.0. When a cloud engineer uses AWS CloudFormation to attempt to peer the application VPC with the shared services VPC, an error message indicates a peering failure. Which factors could cause this error? (Choose two.)
o: The IPv4 CIDR ranges of the two VPCs overlap
The VPCs are not in the same Region
One or both accounts do not have access to an Internet gateway
One of the VPCs was not shared through AWS Resource Access Manager
The IAM role in the peer accepter account does not have the correct permissions

w.y: VPC peering fails if the IPv4 CIDRs overlap; 10.10.0.0/16 would contain 10.10.10.0/24. For cross-account peering with CloudFormation, the accepter account must supply an IAM role (PeerRoleArn) that allows ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection. Inter-Region peering is supported, so the Region difference is not the cause.

o.A: Correct: peering is not allowed between VPCs with overlapping IPv4 CIDR blocks.
o.B: Inter-Region VPC peering is supported, so different Regions do not cause the failure.
o.C: VPC peering does not need an internet gateway.
o.D: Peering does not require sharing VPCs through AWS RAM; RAM shares subnets, which is a different feature.
o.E: Correct: CloudFormation cross-account peering needs a peer role in the accepter account with permission to accept the connection.

s: Peer with a VPC in another AWS account - AWS CloudFormation
